trust_decision.summary: Mutations and traversals of the process-global policy_cache linked list must be serialised by policy_semaphore. At the pinned commit SetMagickSecurityPolicy appends user policies to policy_cache without that lock, while readers walk the list and fill arrays sized from an element count.

landing_point.why: The summary names concurrent security-policy access; SetMagickSecurityPolicy is the only runtime writer of policy_cache, and it calls LoadPolicyCache there without policy_semaphore.

fix_sites.entry_point: MagickCore SetMagickSecurityPolicy(); also reached via MagickWand MagickSetSecurityPolicy() (MagickWand/magick-property.c:2948) and Magick++ Magick::SetSecurityPolicy() (Magick++/lib/Functions.cpp:61)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches one site. The MagickWand and Magick++ wrappers reach it unchanged, so they are not separate sites.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The reader functions already take policy_semaphore before they walk the list (MagickCore/policy.c:409, :505), so once the writer is locked they look safe. The element count is read before the lock (MagickCore/policy.c:405-406, :501-502), but that read is easy to miss because it sits inside the allocation-size expression.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: After the append, SetMagickSecurityPolicy must still apply user resource limits through SetMagickSecurityPolicyValue -> SetMagickResourceLimit, which calls GetPolicyValue -> GetPolicyInfo and takes policy_semaphore again. Semaphores are non-recursive pthread mutexes, so a fix that holds the lock across the whole function, or wraps IsPolicyCacheInstantiated in a reader, self-deadlocks. User limits must also still lower the configured limits.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: MagickCore/policy.c:1449-1456, MagickCore/policy.c:1532, MagickCore/resource.c:1436, MagickCore/resource.c:1466, MagickCore/policy.c:333, MagickCore/policy.c:745

O6_input_shapes: XML policy string with <policy> elements passed to SetMagickSecurityPolicy (the only shape; the fix does not depend on input content)

O7_producer.where: MagickCore/policy.c:1083-1284 (LoadPolicyCache appends PolicyInfo into policy_cache at :1201)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GetPolicyInfoList sizes policies[] from GetNumberOfElementsInLinkedList(policy_cache) before taking policy_semaphore, then fills it under the lock. An append in between overruns the array; the published fix does not close this window.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The loop that fills the array is already locked, and the fix locks the writer, so the reader looks covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 1000 lines above the fix site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GetPolicyList has the same pattern: the count is read outside the lock at allocation, and the array is filled under the lock (heap overflow of char** policies[]).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the same as GetPolicyInfoList, and nothing in-tree calls it except external users of the public API.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ListPolicyInfo (CLI `-list policy`) consumes GetPolicyInfoList, so it reaches the same overrun.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a diagnostic listing feature, not a security check.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; CLI callers in MagickWand/mogrify.c:7259 and MagickWand/operation.c:5286

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second runtime writer, such as a policy reload or include path that appends to policy_cache through LoadPolicyCache without policy_semaphore
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: LoadPolicyCache takes any list and does no locking itself; AcquirePolicyCache (:204-213) already calls it in a loop, so a 'reload policy' API is a plausible maintainer addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A lookup helper that counts or snapshots policy_cache outside the lock, for example a GetPolicyInfo variant returning all matches
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It would copy the existing GetPolicyInfoList shape, including its count-before-lock idiom.

O9_family: race condition / TOCTOU on shared global cache (CWE-362) leading to heap buffer overflow

O10_build.project_tests: No policy-specific tests found under tests/, Magick++/tests or oss-fuzz; the fix diff adds no tests. Any behavioural test needs a multithreaded harness (SetMagickSecurityPolicy racing GetPolicyInfoList), which is nondeterministic unless instrumented.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the LoadPolicyCache call in SetMagickSecurityPolicy with policy_semaphore (the published fix) and stop, leaving the count-before-lock allocations in GetPolicyInfoList/GetPolicyList.

out_of_scope_notes: SetMagickSecurityPolicy never calls IsPolicyCacheInstantiated, so policy_cache may be NULL at MagickCore/policy.c:1436; AppendValueToLinkedList asserts non-NULL (MagickCore/linked-list.c:109). Not pursued.
SetHeadElementInLinkedList (MagickCore/linked-list.c:1015-1040) moves an element to the head without updating tail; a later append may then misbehave. Not a locking issue; not pursued.
Other config caches (type, delegate, magic, locale) use the same count-then-iterate idiom on different sinks; outside this advisory's scope.
unverified: As given, the published fix line fix.diff:142 `UnlockSemaphoreInfo(policy_semaphore)` has no semicolon and would not compile; a follow-up commit may exist, but none was checked.
It is not confirmed that the advisory's heap overflow is specifically the GetPolicyInfoList/GetPolicyList array overrun; this is inferred from code structure.
Repo size in MB was not measured.
present_in_latest is unknown for all O8 routes (no latest release provided).
Deterministic testability of the race was not assessed; hidden tests may need fault injection or many-iteration stress.
